_about:
WHICH STAGE EACH BLUEPRINT STEP BELONGS TO, AND WHERE IN THE APP IT IS DONE - a sidecar, for the same reason steps.priority.json and steps.tanglish.json are.

docs/BLUEPRINT-REALIGN-PLAN.md, revision 3, section 3. The feature blueprint used to be four 'phases' (Story 01-12, Pre-Production 13-24, Production 25-28, Post 29-32) that were not the app's five stages: there was no Screenplay, and Story > Feature Blueprint opened on 'Phase 02 Pre-Production', a stage inside a stage. It is five PARTS now, one per stage, and the step order and numbers are unchanged - only the boundaries moved (11, 12 and 13 are Part II, Screenplay).

WHY A SIDECAR. steps.feature.json and steps.short.json are REGENERATED by `npm run extract` from legacy/, so anything written into a step there is destroyed by the next extraction. One file, all namespaces, merged at render time by src/ui/step-stages.js.

KEYS are `<namespace>:<step id>` exactly like the priority sidecar. The feature page renders steps 01-24 under `feature` and 25-32 under `production`; the short film is `short`. Interludes (sections that are not steps and hold no step number) are keyed the same way by their section id.

`stage` is a navigation.json PHASE id (story, screenplay, preprod, production, post), or a list of them where one step really spans two. Its label and its hue are read from navigation.json at render time, never written here - the hue class is `.sh-ph-<phase.hue>`, and a wrong family fails silently by design (CLAUDE.md, the --hue trap).

`part` is the blueprint part the step sits in; for the feature it equals the stage's position among the five. `lock: true` marks the short film's final step, which locks the screenplay after the festival plan and belongs to no part.

`tools` are navigation.json MODULE ids for the 'Do this in...' row; label and href come from navigation.json (src/lib/navmodel.js allModules()), so a renamed module renames its button. An object entry is a deep link a module id cannot express: `module` (whose label leads) or `place` (a global destination's href, whose label leads), plus the `href` and a `sub` label. An id that resolves to nothing is reported once with console.warn and skipped - a dead button is worse than a missing one.

`readout` names a live line derived from the scene, script, schedule and contact models (src/ui/step-stages.js). It is computed when the page renders and when it becomes visible again, and STORED NOWHERE.

`parts.feature` is the order the feature page lays its parts out in and the cover each one opens with. The ids vol-1, vol-2, phase-3 and phase-4 are kept because they are linked from elsewhere and their cover fields are users' saved work; vol-2 now opens Part III. part-2 is new and has no fields.
